documents_checked.text:
Feedback on Student work may be generated through self and peer review and assessment so
that Students have an opportunity to practise applying criteria and standards to their own
work and that of others. The following must be met:
peer review and peer assessment processes must be designed to ensure that Students can be
treated with respect by other Students, and must be supported by clear guidelines and criteria
for the review;
Students must always receive Feedback on their self and peer reviews and assessments to
assist them in calibrating their judgement to match discipline standards;
Self and peer assessment is to be used for Formative Assessment purposes only – the grading
of Student work is the Unit Coordinator’s responsibility; and
if Students are required to generate constructive Feedback for a peer, the quality of such
Feedback may be a component of Summative Assessment.

documents_checked.text:
Assessment Panels
Each School must have an Assessment Panel comprising Teaching Staff from the Course Stage,
and other Staff as determined by the Executive Dean of the School (e.g. Course Coordinator)
and have oversight by the Associate Dean (Teaching and Learning). The Assessment Panel will
have sufficient subject matter expertise relevant to the Course.
Where Student performance is assessed across different locations, Schools, providers or
Courses, the Course Coordinator(s) must be included in the Assessment Panel.
The Assessment Panel is to holistically evaluate a combined selection of evidence in order to
confirm a Student’s progression and completion with reference to the CLOs.
The Assessment Panel may conduct an informal viva with a Student where they deem it
necessary for Student Identity Verification or to verify CLO progress and achievement.
The Assessment Panel will provide each Student with feedback on Assessments, describing
their progression towards achievement of the CLOs and providing advice about how to best
approach their learning throughout the remainder of their Course.
Consistent with a criterion and standards referenced approach, where grades are provided, the
allocation of a grade must reflect the level of Student attainment in relation to Benchmarked
Standards. Any scaling of marks must be justifiable by reference to Benchmarked Standards
and endorsed by the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Education).
Consensus moderation must be employed by Assessment Panels to ensure reliable judgements
in relation to Benchmarked Standards during all phases of the Assessment cycle.

case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: N154 restricts peer assessment to formative purposes only, makes the Unit Coordinator the accountable grader, requires Assessment Panel moderation, and provides formal appeal rights, preventing unreviewed AI evaluations from determining binding marks.
case_summary.case_note: ECU prohibits unreviewed peer or AI evaluations from determining binding academic marks under N154, which restricts peer assessment to formative use only and assigns grading responsibility to the Unit Coordinator. Final grades must undergo Assessment Panel consensus moderation and are subject to student appeal rights. Protocol v1.1 was adopted after preliminary review.

supporting_passages.text:
This policy applies to:
Complaints made by prospective, current and former Students or members of the public about
the University or University-related conduct, whether occurring in Australia or overseas; and
all persons involved in making, responding to, managing or resolving those Complaints.
Where legislation or another University or external framework provides a specific process for
dealing with all or part of a matter, the University may refer or manage that matter under the
applicable process. This includes matters concerning academic review or appeal, public
interest disclosures, misconduct, staff performance, privacy, employment or workplace
grievances, the ECU Student Guild, and third-party organisations.
This does not prevent the University from considering a distinct Complaint about its
administration of, or response to, the matter.
Where a matter engages more than one framework, the University will determine whether the
relevant issues are to be managed separately, sequentially, concurrently or in a coordinated
manner and will inform the Complainant of the applicable pathway.

Assessment Panels
Each School must have an Assessment Panel comprising Teaching Staff from the Course Stage,
and other Staff as determined by the Executive Dean of the School (e.g. Course Coordinator)
and have oversight by the Associate Dean (Teaching and Learning). The Assessment Panel will
have sufficient subject matter expertise relevant to the Course.
Where Student performance is assessed across different locations, Schools, providers or
Courses, the Course Coordinator(s) must be included in the Assessment Panel.
The Assessment Panel is to holistically evaluate a combined selection of evidence in order to
confirm a Student’s progression and completion with reference to the CLOs.
The Assessment Panel may conduct an informal viva with a Student where they deem it
necessary for Student Identity Verification or to verify CLO progress and achievement.
The Assessment Panel will provide each Student with feedback on Assessments, describing
their progression towards achievement of the CLOs and providing advice about how to best
approach their learning throughout the remainder of their Course.
Consistent with a criterion and standards referenced approach, where grades are provided, the
allocation of a grade must reflect the level of Student attainment in relation to Benchmarked
Standards. Any scaling of marks must be justifiable by reference to Benchmarked Standards
and endorsed by the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Education).
Consensus moderation must be employed by Assessment Panels to ensure reliable judgements
in relation to Benchmarked Standards during all phases of the Assessment cycle.

Appeals
In addition to any review mechanisms set out in these procedures, Students have the right to
appeal in accordance with the Admission, Enrolment and Academic Progress Rules.
